During my initial visit for a cleaning, I was told I had four small cavities, so I started treatment. Each cavity treatment costs 800 baht. I was told that although it wasn't visible on the X-ray, it had progressed when they opened my teeth, and it cost 2500 baht for one tooth. I don't know if that was true or not, as I have no proof. It's possible they drilled more than necessary just to charge me. One dentist made me buy a disposable instrument to keep my mouth open for 100 baht. Isn't that something the hospital should provide? When the doctor and dental assistant interrupted the treatment and left the room chatting (with laughter) without any explanation, I was left alone with my mouth open, not knowing what was going on, and I felt very anxious. (I realized then that the interpreter wasn't with me the whole time during the treatment.) They said they were changing the drill because it wasn't working properly. Why didn't they check before the treatment? The treatment for two cavities took two hours. I was told they were small cavities, but the total cost for two treatments was about 7000 baht. I realized again that choosing a trustworthy dentist is more important than whether they speak Japanese. I'm currently going to a highly skilled dental clinic (with English-speaking staff) near Rama 9 station and I'm very satisfied.
